name: Car Maintenance
summary: Do your own oil changes, brakes, filters and diagnostics, and understand what's happening under the bonnet.
safety: Never work under a car held up only by a jack. Use axle stands on firm, level ground.

name: Classic Car Restoration
summary: Bring a classic car back from rust to road through bodywork, mechanics, wiring and trim.

name: Car Detailing
summary: Wash, decontaminate, machine-polish and protect paintwork until the reflections are mirror-clear.

name: Car Modifying & Tuning
summary: Improve handling and power with suspension, tyres, intakes and ECU maps, and measure every change.
safety: Keep modifications road-legal, and tell your insurer about every one.

name: Kit Car Building
summary: Build a road-legal sports car from a kit and donor parts in your own garage.
safety: The finished car must pass your country's inspection before it can be driven on the road.

name: Driving Stick
summary: Learn clutch control, hill starts and smooth gear changes, and eventually heel-and-toe downshifts.

gear: A manual car and a patient teacher

name: Advanced Driving
summary: Take roadcraft beyond the test: observation, planning, smooth control and staying safe at any speed.

name: Track Days
summary: Drive your own car on a real circuit and learn racing lines, braking points and car control.
safety: Check tyres, brakes and fluids first, wear a helmet and book instruction for your first day. Normal car insurance rarely covers track use.

name: Autocross & Autotests
summary: Run timed laps through tight cone courses in a car park. It is the cheapest way into motorsport.
safety: Wear a helmet and run only at organised events with marshals.

name: Karting
summary: Race low, fast karts and learn racing lines, overtaking and race craft, the first step for most racing drivers.

name: Drifting
summary: Hold a car in a controlled slide with throttle, steering and weight transfer, all in a cloud of tyre smoke.
safety: Drift only at organised events on closed venues, never on public roads.

name: Off-Roading
summary: Drive 4x4s over rocks, mud and river crossings, with line choice, tyre pressures and recovery skills.
safety: Never go alone. Carry recovery gear, learn safe winching and stay on legal routes.

name: Motorcycling
summary: Get licensed and learn to ride well, from slow-speed control to cornering and long-distance touring.
safety: Train with a qualified instructor, wear full protective gear on every ride and assume drivers can't see you.

name: Motorcycle Maintenance
summary: Service your own bike: chain, brakes, oil, valves and carburettors, guided by the workshop manual.

name: Motocross
summary: Race dirt bikes over jumps, ruts and berms on purpose-built tracks.
safety: Wear a helmet, boots, goggles and body armour, and ride within your limits. Jumps cause most serious injuries.

name: Electric Unicycles
summary: Ride a self-balancing single wheel by learning to mount, lean, carve and handle speed.
safety: Wear a helmet and pads, ride within sensible speeds and check local laws on where you can ride.

name: Bike Maintenance
summary: Fix punctures, tune gears and brakes, true wheels and keep your bike running silently.

name: Bicycle Frame Building
summary: Cut, mitre and braze steel tubes into a frame built to fit your body exactly.
safety: Learn torch work on a course first, and work with good ventilation and a fire extinguisher nearby.

name: Bikepacking
summary: Pack light frame bags and ride multi-day off-road routes, camping wherever the trail takes you.

name: RC Cars
summary: Race, bash and crawl radio-controlled cars, then tune their suspension, gearing and electronics.
safety: Charge LiPo batteries in a fireproof bag and never leave them charging unattended.

name: RC Planes
summary: Build and fly radio-controlled aircraft, from foam trainers to scale warbirds and gliders.
safety: Learn at a club field and follow the model aircraft rules where you fly.

name: Learning to Fly
summary: Earn a private pilot's licence and take the controls yourself: circuits, navigation and your first solo.
safety: Train at an approved flight school, and fly within your licence, your currency and the weather limits.

name: Gliding
summary: Fly an engineless sailplane for hours on thermals and ridge lift, reading the sky to stay up.
safety: Learn at a gliding club with qualified instructors, and follow its checks and launch procedures.

name: Powerboating
summary: Skipper a motorboat with confidence: handling, mooring, rules of the road and reading the water.
safety: Wear a life jacket, check the weather and tides, and take a recognised course before you skipper.

name: Canal Boating
summary: Cruise canals at walking pace, working locks, swing bridges and tunnels as you go.
safety: Keep the boat clear of the cill in locks, and never jump between the boat and the bank.

name: Boat Building
summary: Build a canoe, dinghy or rowing boat from plans using stitch-and-glue, strip-planking or traditional methods.
safety: Wear gloves and a respirator when working with epoxy, and ventilate the workshop.

name: Engine Rebuilding
summary: Strip an engine to the block, then measure, machine and reassemble it to factory tolerances.

name: Small Engine Repair
summary: Bring mowers, chainsaws and scooters back to life by cleaning carburettors, replacing plugs and tuning them.
safety: Work in a ventilated space, disconnect the spark plug before touching blades and store fuel safely.

name: EV Conversion
summary: Swap a classic car's engine for an electric motor and battery pack for silent, instant torque.
safety: High-voltage battery packs can kill. Learn high-voltage safety, use insulated tools and have the conversion inspected before road use.

name: Lathe & Mill Machining
summary: Turn and mill metal parts to a hundredth of a millimetre for tools, engines and models.
safety: Never wear gloves, loose sleeves or jewellery near a lathe, always remove the chuck key and wear eye protection.

name: Watchmaking & Repair
summary: Service mechanical watches: strip, clean, oil and regulate tiny movements under a loupe.

name: Trainspotting
summary: Log locomotives, photograph heritage steam and learn the railway's classes, liveries and routes.
safety: Stay behind the platform edge and never trespass on the railway.

name: Plane Spotting
summary: Identify aircraft types and airlines, track flights live and photograph landings at airport viewpoints.
